critical_code_review_comments: routes/towing.py complete_request — the credit-operator branch contains the condition `req.get('status') != 'completed'` AFTER the update that already sets status='completed'. Because the freshly-fetched `req` dict is from BEFORE the update_one call (status was 'en_route'/'arrived' at fetch time), the guard relies on the in-memory dict; it works idempotently only because the wallet debit guard above (`req.get('payment_status') != 'paid'`) already skipped (no debit happens twice). However on a parallel race (two concurrent /complete calls) both would read status=en_route, both pass the guard, and BOTH credit the operator. Recommend using atomic find_one_and_update for the completion step (set status='completed' only if current status not 'completed') and only proceed with the wallet credit + revenue insert when modified_count==1. Current test passes only because requests are sequential.

operator_documents endpoint allows ANY string for insurance/license/id_card URLs — no schema validation or URL/type check; a malicious user could store javascript: or arbitrary text. Add pydantic validator or url type.
admin_verify_operator accepts `reason` as free string with no length limit — consider max length.
Commission setting PUT does not record an audit trail (who changed, when, previous value). Recommended for finance compliance.
/admin/towing/revenue has no date range filter — will get expensive over time; add since/until query params and an index on towing_revenue.created_at.

operator_me computes earnings via fallback `j.get('operator_earning', total*(1-pct))` — historic jobs completed BEFORE iter394 won't have operator_earning persisted but will be back-computed with TODAY's commission, which can drift if commission_pct changes later. Acceptable, but consider a migration to backfill operator_earning on legacy rows.
Operator notification on verify uses best-effort try/except Exception:pass — should log on failure.
